_comment: Declarative Netbird access-control policy for the private management mesh. Parallels modules/network/tailscale-policy.json. Import this file into the Netbird management console (Setup Keys → Policies, or via the Netbird API at https://api.netbird.io/api/v1/policies). The schema differs from Tailscale: Netbird uses a Policy with rules of the form {name, sources, destinations, protocol, action, ports, portRange}. The deny-by-default design and the printserver-source-denial invariant are preserved.

groups.name: private
groups.description: Personal private fleet — UwU and UwU-Server. Owns the bulk of the mesh services.

groups.name: work
groups.description: Work laptop — TSBW-W01800. One-way trust into private for SSH and Hermes services.

groups.name: personal
groups.description: Explicitly approved personal devices (Android phone, etc.). One-way trust into private for SSH and Hermes services.

groups.name: printserver
groups.description: Print server group — RESERVED. Projet-Printserver is no longer enrolled on Netbird (2026-08-09 user decision: print server stays on a plain LAN path, no mesh). The group is kept so any future device that joins the `printserver` netbird group inherits the deny-by-default-source invariant: never appears in any `sources` list. May receive inbound SSH from private/work/personal only.

rules.name: private-to-all-mesh-services
rules.description: Private nodes can reach every other group on the management ports. OpenSSH (22), Hermes WebUI (8080), Hermes Mobile Bridge (8642/9119/9131), Gitea (443), AdGuard (3000), and a handful of utility ports (3001/3002/3030/19999/28981).

rules.name: work-to-private-mesh-services
rules.description: Work laptop reaches the same services private can reach, but only on private nodes.

rules.name: personal-to-private-mesh-services
rules.description: Personal devices (phone, etc.) reach the same services work can reach, but only on private nodes.

rules._comment_invariant: There is NO rule with `sources: [printserver]`. The print server is deny-by-default-source: it may only receive inbound SSH from private/work/personal nodes (covered by the three accept rules above). No explicit deny rule is needed in Netbird policy — the absence of a source clause is the invariant. Tests in tests/netbird-mesh-regressions.py assert this invariant.

_invariants.no_autogroup_member_equivalent: Netbird has no implicit 'all members of the org' grant equivalent. The four groups above are the only sources of authority. New peers that join without a group assignment cannot reach any service.
_invariants.no_printserver_as_source: None of the rule sources include `printserver`. The print server is a sink only.
_invariants.ssh_is_the_only_trust_path: OpenSSH (port 22) is the only authentication path. Netbird is the encrypted wire; jaide_nixos is the only authorised human key. The pin of the OpenSSH host key is the trust root per docs/netbird-mesh.md.
